claims.text: The charge fails POL-NS-01 at the first limb: the trip record contains no driver 'arrived' event at all — trip_record.arrived_at is null and the trip status is CANCELLED_BY_RIDER. POL-NS-01 is deliberately conjunctive, so breaking this single limb is enough to make the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee not chargeable under it, and the inquiry moves to the refund clauses.

Limb (d) fails independently of arrival. The trip was terminated by the rider, not the driver (cancelled_by 'RIDER'), and the cancellation_reason_code is RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, which is not one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises — RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT — and is a rider-side change-of-mind code rather than a driver no-show code. The required condition that the driver terminated the trip at or after the elapsed dwell therefore cannot be met on this record.

The driver never came near the pickup point. On his own trace, the closest he gets to the pin across the whole twenty-four minutes is 1,352.34 m (derived.driver_track.min_distance_m), against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius fixed by the fee schedule and applied in POL-NS-02; his track runs out to 3,120.37 m. The derived arrival block counts 0 qualifying in-radius fixes out of 145 driver fixes, so no qualifying in-radius fix exists at any point in the window preceding the cancellation: the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and POL-NS-02 entitles the rider to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

This is not a wrong-entrance or wrong-block case, so POL-NS-03 cannot soften the outcome or divert any money to the driver. That clause requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell at a point not more than 400 m from the pickup pin (the wrong_entrance_ceiling_m). The nearest point on the driver's track is 1,352.34 m away, more than three times that ceiling. There is no venue-identity question to decide either — both venue_id fields are null and registered_pickup_points is 1 — and the distance test alone settles it.

The waiting-period arithmetic is a clean shortfall. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0.0; qualifying_fix_count 0) against the 300-second minimum for a STANDARD pickup zone, a shortfall of 300 seconds (derived.arrival.accumulated_dwell.shortfall_sec). Under POL-NS-06 the fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

Nothing in the bundle excuses that shortfall. The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00605-01, is MISSING: it has no payload and carries weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT ('No advisory covers the pickup road in this window'), and I disclose that impairment because I rely on the absence itself. POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed or the minimum relaxed; no such advisory exists here, so limb (i) is unavailable and no interval can be accumulated.

The trace contains no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, and the driver's speed fixes are either 0.0 or 63.8-66.3 km/h — stationary or in fast motion, never a slow approach to a kerb. POL-NS-05 limb (ii) addresses precisely this state of affairs: where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver in the ruling's referrals list. This record has no arrival marker at all, which is stronger than a false one, and any arrival marker asserted on these coordinates would be false under the clause's 300 m test.

The artifacts carrying the deciding facts are clean, so no impairment discount applies to them. EV-GPS-00605 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with 145 fixes at a 10 s cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps array; EV-TRIP-00605 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0. None of the POL-NS-08(a) to (d) defects — clock skew, trace gap, truncated chat or fare mismatch — is present, so the GPS findings stand at full weight and confidence on the deciding facts is not capped below the 0.70 platform floor.

The contested amount is exactly the cancellation-fee line and it is the correct figure. EV-FARE-00605 shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and 4.00 is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00) under the fee_schedule resolution rule, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and nothing turns on the tie. Refunding the cancellation-fee line in full returns the entire SGD 4.00 contested; no booking or platform fee rides on this cancelled trip.

Driver compensation is not engaged. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here two limbs of POL-NS-01 fail and POL-NS-06 mandates the full refund, so the clause never opens and the anti-farming check is never reached. The driver's explanation of a frozen app supplies no arrival event and no in-geofence position, and his own telemetry shows him between 1,352 m and 3,120 m from the pin throughout; the SGD 4.00 belongs back with the rider, not converted into a payout.

No escalation trigger is available on these facts, and escalation would hold the SGD 4.00 rather than return it. POL-NS-09(c) needs two or more no-show disputes between this same rider and this same driver in the trailing 90 days — rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0 — and POL-NS-09(d) reads rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d, which is 0. I rely only on those named fields; the profiles' other entries (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_no_show_flags, prior_deviation_flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not grounds of decision here.

The rider was at the pin the whole time, and her account is corroborated rather than contradicted. The rider track carries 147 fixes whose greatest distance from the pin is 14.92 m (derived.rider_presence.max_distance_m), well inside the 100 m rider-presence radius for STANDARD that POL-NS-04(c) applies, and trip_record records four rider-placed in-app calls at 18:36:40, 18:40:40, 18:45:40 and 18:50:40, every one of them unanswered. I do not overstate POL-NS-04: limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating chat message, and the chat log holds none (0 messages, consistent with trip_record.chat_message_count of 0, so no POL-NS-08(c) chat defect arises), so that clause's own exoneration route cannot be run on this record. The refund follows from POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 in any event, and the driver's total silence on both channels is consistent with his never having approached the pickup.

The outcome the evidence supports is FULL_REFUND of the whole SGD 4.00 to the filing rider and no driver compensation. POL-GEN-03 defines FULL_REFUND as the filing party being entirely right with the entire contested amount returned, and that is this case: the rider was present at the pin for the full twenty-four minutes with a track never more than 14.92 m from it, the driver's own trace never brings him within 1,352.34 m, and the conditions that would make the no-show fee chargeable never came close to being satisfied.

claims.text: The one thing the driver can properly say about the money is that the amount is right. EV-FARE-00605 charges a cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 and a total_charged of SGD 4.00, which is exactly the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under the fee_schedule resolution rule, with the STANDARD dimension governing the tie. The ledger line therefore reconciles with the schedule and no fare-integrity defect exists under POL-NS-08(d); whatever becomes of the charge, the quantum itself is not attackable and I do not invite the judge to substitute a different figure.

The false-arrival branch does not touch this driver. EV-TRIP-00605 records arrived_at as null and started_at as null, and the derived arrival block built from EV-GPS-00605 reports arrived_at null with a qualifying_fix_count of 0. POL-NS-05 bites only where an 'arrived' event carries a timestamp at which the trace puts the driver more than 300 m out or still in motion; with no 'arrived' event at all there is no marker to test, so the driver never falsely marked arrival and the POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral should not be written against him.

I do not press chargeability on the anchor clause, and candour requires me to say why. POL-NS-01 requires all four limbs, and two of them fail on the face of EV-TRIP-00605: there is no driver 'arrived' event for the trip, so limb (a) fails, and the trip was terminated by the rider on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND with cancelled_by RIDER, not by the driver on RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, so limb (d) fails as well. The driver's explanation that his app froze does not repair either limb: POL-NS-01 is mechanical and contains no device-fault excuse, and in any event his own trace runs at 100 percent coverage with no gaps and 145 fixes, which sits awkwardly with a frozen app.

Limb (b) cannot be carried either, and the figures are not marginal. On the driver's own 145-fix trace, EV-GPS-00605 puts his minimum distance from the pickup pin at 1,352.3 m and his mean distance at 3,032.5 m, with qualifying_fix_count of 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0.0 seconds. There is accordingly no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes before the 18:54:40 cancellation, POL-NS-02's arrival test is unmet on admissible fixes, and the consequence POL-NS-02 draws — that the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation-fee line — is not something I can resist on this record.

There is no dwell to count against the minimum either. The STANDARD minimum is 300 seconds and EV-GPS-00605 reports the longest qualifying in-geofence run as 0.0 seconds against a shortfall of the full 300 seconds, so the waiting-period arithmetic under POL-NS-06 is not seriously contestable and the fee is not defensible on that route.

For completeness, neither door under POL-NS-06(i) opens for the driver. The trace shows run_count 0 and zero in-geofence intervals, so there is no second interval there to add to a first, and the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-00605-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT because no advisory covers the pickup road in this window. I say plainly that I do not assert that missing artifact: POL-NS-06(i) requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, a MISSING advisory makes the limb unavailable, and pressing the limb against a MISSING artifact would trigger POL-NS-09 rather than exonerate anyone.

The one clause that could still have rescued the driver's side, POL-NS-03, fails on its own distance ceiling. It applies only where the trace shows the driver stationary for the required dwell at a point outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pickup pin, and EV-GPS-00605 puts the driver's closest approach at 1,352.3 m, more than three times that ceiling. There is also no venue_id on the pickup or the dropoff in EV-TRIP-00605, so no venue match could corroborate a wrong-face-of-the-same-venue case in any event and the distance test governs alone. The 50 percent pin-ambiguity goodwill under POL-NS-03(ii) is therefore unavailable and I do not ask for it.

POL-NS-07's payout is equally out of reach. It is available only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and here POL-NS-01 fails at limbs (a) to (d) while POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 both displace it, so no compensation can be awarded. The anti-farming check does not change that: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against completed_trips_30d of 110, so the 4-or-more limb and the 0.08 rate limb are both unmet. I confine this submission to those two named fields, as POL-NS-07 and POL-GEN-01 require, and I make no use of rating, acceptance_rate, account age, lifetime counters or any other profile field as a ground of decision.

I do not seek escalation under POL-NS-09, because no trigger is genuinely present. Limb (b) needs two admissible artifacts that contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, and EV-TRIP-00605 and EV-GPS-00605 agree rather than conflict — both record that no arrival occurred. Limbs (c) and (d) do not fire either (disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and the anti-farming check does not trip), and no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d), so limb (e) is not in play. The honest consequence is that this dispute is decided on the GPS facts, not by sending it to a human reviewer.

The rider's coordination route through POL-NS-04 does not open on this record: limb (a) requires at least one rider message in the chat_log during the waiting window, and EV-CHAT-00605 returns message_count 0 with an empty message array, matching the trip_record.chat_message_count of 0. I acknowledge candidly that the record holds four in-app calls placed by the rider at 18:36:40, 18:40:40, 18:45:40 and 18:50:40, each recorded in EV-TRIP-00605 as unanswered, and that those calls are the most adverse facts against the driver on this trip; but they are voice calls, not chat messages, and they do not satisfy limb (a).
